title: Strengthen national targets
why: Set 2030 and 2035 goals in line with 1.5 °C, so policy has something real to aim at.

title: Stop fossil fuel expansion
why: No new oil and gas projects, end fossil fuel subsidies and avoid locking in gas.

title: Scale up clean power
why: Build solar, wind, grids and storage fast enough to replace fossil power, not just add to it.

title: Phase out coal
why: Set a firm date to close coal plants, with support for affected workers.

title: Publish a long-term plan
why: A clear, transparent roadmap to net zero, with the data behind it.

title: Electrify transport and buildings
why: Electric cars, efficient buildings and clean heating and cooling.

title: Put a real price on carbon
why: Tight caps and enforced carbon prices, so polluting costs more.

title: Fund the transition
why: Pay for clean energy at home, pay a fair share abroad, and stop financing fossil fuels.

title: Protect forests and land
why: Stop deforestation and count land-use emissions honestly.

title: Cut methane and farm emissions
why: Tackle methane from coal mines, livestock and farming.

title: Clean up heavy industry
why: Make low-emission steel and cement the norm.

title: Cut and report weapons-usable material
why: The less weapons-usable material there is, and the more openly it is counted, the fewer places it can be stolen from.

title: End reprocessing and secure spent fuel
why: Reprocessing spent fuel creates new weapons-usable material. Permanent storage keeps it out of reach.

title: Strengthen people and cyber security
why: Insiders and hackers are among the hardest threats to nuclear sites. Many countries still have weak personnel and cyber rules.

title: Independent oversight and testing
why: Security that is regulated, tested and self-assessed every year is more likely to work when it matters.

title: Join the nuclear security treaties
why: Treaty membership makes each country's commitments binding and open to review.

title: Reduce the risk of nuclear use
why: Hotlines, warning notices and more decision time lower the chance that a mistake or a false alarm leads to use.

title: Restart arms control talks
why: With the last US-Russia treaty gone, there are no agreed limits or inspections on the two largest arsenals.

title: Protect 30% of every land habitat
why: Set aside at least 30% of each type of land habitat, so protection covers the full range of nature and not only the easy places.

title: Stop habitat loss and degradation
why: Plan how land is used so the most important natural areas are kept intact.

title: Pull threatened species back from the edge
why: Halt human-caused extinctions and help threatened species recover.

title: Keep ecosystems connected and climate-ready
why: Restore damaged ecosystems and keep habitats joined up so wildlife can adapt.

title: Redirect harmful subsidies to nature
why: Stop paying for activity that harms nature and back what helps it.

title: Get enough affordable food within reach
why: Make sure people who go hungry can get and afford enough food, and keep conflict from cutting them off from it.

title: Protect children's growth in the first 1,000 days
why: Reach mothers and young children with nutrition support from pregnancy to age two, when stunting takes hold.

title: Find and treat acute malnutrition early
why: Screen children for wasting and give treatment, such as therapeutic food, before they become seriously ill.

title: Cut child deaths linked to undernutrition
why: Deliver the proven nutrition and health basics that keep undernourished children alive.

title: Keep hunger data and early warning funded
why: Keep measuring hunger and nutrition so crises are seen early, even when aid budgets shrink.

title: Reach children who have had no vaccines
why: Find the children who have never had a single routine vaccine and bring them into regular care.

title: Help children finish their first-year vaccines
why: Make sure children who start their vaccines come back for the third DTP dose.

title: Give every child a first measles dose
why: Reach every infant with the first dose of measles vaccine.

title: Give every child the second measles dose
why: Offer the second measles dose in the routine schedule and make sure children come back for it.

title: Keep vaccines funded and coverage tracked
why: Keep paying for vaccines and for the surveys and data that show who is missed, even as aid budgets shrink.

title: Protect the people AI could leave out
why: Cover gender equality, children's rights and local languages in AI rules, and act on them (GIRAI's Inclusion and Diversity dimension).

title: Make AI fair, open and overseen by people
why: Require fairness, transparency, human oversight and reporting of environmental impact (GIRAI's Ethics and Sustainability dimension).

title: Protect workers and build AI skills
why: Pair AI skills and literacy programmes with protections for workers (GIRAI's Labour and Skills dimension).

title: Keep people safe and give them a way to complain
why: Assess risks before AI is used, tackle AI-driven misinformation and violence, and give people a route to redress (GIRAI's Trust and Safety dimension).

title: Be open about how government uses AI
why: Disclose the AI systems government uses, buy AI under fair and accountable rules, and include civil society (GIRAI's AI Use in Public Service dimension).
